analysis.title: GS Stankard - Eq Positioning and Key Levels 16 Nov 2026
key_insights: CTAs simulated to have sold $23bn of SPX over the past week ($46.5bn over the past month) and are estimated mildly short $3bn of SPX as of Friday's close.

SPX price action into the end of last week flipped medium-term CTA momentum positive again, implying modest buying this week. Spot sits near the threshold level, so flow forecasts may vary until a clearer trend forms.
CTA flow forecast over the next week: flat tape buyers $22.97B ($9.86B into the US), up tape buyers $30.78B ($16.1B into the US), down tape sellers $6.07B ($5.23B out of the US).
CTA flow forecast over the next month: flat tape buyers $13.87B ($8.01B US), up tape buyers $89.1B ($54.04B US), down tape sellers $122.97B ($20.31B US).
GS key SPX pivot levels: short term 7,657, medium term 7,555, long term 7,133 (data as of 9 Nov 2026). A 1x std-dev market move is 1.62% in one week and 3.78% in one month.
GS Prime Brokerage: global equities were net sold (-0.7 SDs 1-year) as de-grossing increased, with long sales outpacing short covers 2.8 to 1.
Single stocks were net sold for a 9th straight week, while macro products were net bought for a 4th straight week, driven by short covers and to a lesser extent long buys.
Info Tech was by far the most $ net sold global and US sector again. The US Info Tech long/short ratio is 1.5 versus a YTD peak of 2.14 in early June, the lowest on record (since 2016).

Energy was the most $ net bought and most risk-on global sector, bought at the fastest pace in 3 months with long buys outpacing short sales 7 to 1. Oil, Gas & Consumable Fuels drove it, while Energy Equipment & Services saw little net activity.

Financials was the most net sold US sector in SD terms (-2.2 SDs 1-year), with long and short sales at about 4 to 1. The % net selling was the largest in 8 months and in the 99th percentile on a 5-year lookback.
Consumer Discretionary was the most $ net bought US sector (+1.0 SDs 1-year), driven by long buys and short covers. The % net buying was the largest in more than 3 months.

Hedge funds net sold US equities for a second straight week (5 of the last 6, -0.4 SDs 1-year), driven by single-stock short sales partly offset by short covers and long buys in macro products. US-listed ETF shorts fell 8.6%, the largest % covering in 7 months, led by Large Cap Equity, Credit and Tech ETFs.
Overall book gross leverage fell 2.1 pts to 312.1% (74th percentile 1-year). Net leverage fell 0.4 pts to 71.4% (3rd percentile). L/S ratio rose 0.1% to 1.593 (4th percentile).
Fundamental L/S net leverage rose 0.1 pts to 45.4%, a 1-year low. Beta-adjusted fundamental net leverage fell 0.2 pts to 57.0%, also a 1-year low.

Buybacks: about 94% of the S&P 500 is in open window, rising to about 95% by the end of the week, with the open period expected to run through early/mid December. 2026 YTD repurchase authorizations are $1.52T. Desk volumes were 1.3x 2025 YTD ADTV, with a 45% open-market / 55% 10b5-1 mix versus 33% / 67% the prior week. GS expects the usual December taper.
